content.text:
I fixed the main layout regression, but the visual tests still fail on both desktop and phone. A smaller text difference remains that I couldn't trace to the code.

**What I fixed:** the `.container` max-width at the 1200px breakpoint in `site/css/styles.css` was `1710px`. I set it back to Bootstrap's `1140px`. With 1710px the navbar and content stretched out and sat in the wrong place. After the change, the navbar, hero, sections, images and footer line up with the approved screenshot.

**What still fails:** all the text renders slightly differently from the approved screenshots:
- The navbar brand, body text and footer are about 1–2% wider than approved. The section headings are about 0.5% narrower.
- On desktop this makes one paragraph wrap onto 2 lines instead of 3 in each section. The page ends up 1826px tall against the approved 1856px.
- On phone the layout matches, and only the glyph spacing differs.

I checked the font settings (family, weight, size, letter-spacing, kerning, optical sizing, text-rendering) and found nothing unusual. The CSS is standard Bootstrap, and every computed value is what it should be. The repo has a single commit, so I couldn't diff against the previous version. A text-spacing change like this could come from a different font build or renderer when the screenshots were approved, rather than from the site code. If you know the font setup changed, regenerating the baselines is the likely fix. If you know of other edits since the last good version, tell me and I'll look at those.

Two untracked folders, `.idea` and `.vscode`, appeared in the repo. I didn't create them and left them alone.

STATUS: NOT DONE
